headline: Samsung smart fridges bricked by firmware update, spoiling food
summary: Samsung's Bespoke AI fridges in Korea are reportedly losing power and stopping function after a SmartThings firmware update, leading to spoiled food and ruined holidays.
details: Samsung's Bespoke AI refrigerators in Korea have been rendered inoperable following a recent firmware update pushed through the SmartThings app. Users reported that their fridges suddenly lost power and stopped functioning immediately after the update, with the SmartThings app showing the devices as offline.

The issue appears to primarily affect four-door Bespoke AI fridges from 2024 or later. Numerous reports on Samsung's Korean community forums detail the problem, with some users stating their fridges were only a year old or less. The malfunction has led to all food inside being spoiled.

The timing of the failures is particularly unfortunate, coinciding with Chuseok, a major Korean holiday celebrating the autumn harvest. This has caused significant distress for customers who relied on their refrigerators for holiday preparations.

Samsung has stopped issuing the problematic update as of September 23rd and is working to address the issues, with some repairs expected by September 24th. A Samsung representative acknowledged the error during a testing process and stated that emergency measures are being prioritized through Samsung Electronics Service Centers.

While Samsung is working on repairs, some users reported initial difficulties reaching support, with claims of limited technicians and potential repair delays extending into October. This has exacerbated frustration among those whose holidays have been disrupted.

This incident highlights the risks associated with increasingly connected appliances. While smart features offer convenience, a faulty update can turn a simple product into a significant problem, potentially spoiling not just food but also essential medications.
